title: Jared Kushner and Affinity Partners
summary: The core facts hold. Trump publicly named Kushner an 'envoy of peace' (19 Feb 2026), and he negotiates alongside Witkoff with no formal title and no financial disclosure. Saudi PIF committed $2B to Affinity in 2021, and the NYT reported in March 2026 that he was seeking $5B or more, largely from Gulf sovereign funds. Two points overreach: PIF is Affinity's largest investor, not just 'one of' them, and 'not subject to' disclosure or divestment is the White House's contested legal position, which CREW is challenging in court. The suggestion that he argues for his own interests in talks is unproven insinuation.

sub_claims.statement: Trump has called Kushner the 'peace envoy'.
sub_claims.finding: At the first Board of Peace meeting on 19 Feb 2026, Trump said 'We're making Jared an envoy also, envoy of peace.' The White House then said the role would not be official.

sub_claims.statement: Kushner takes part in negotiations alongside Steve Witkoff in an unofficial capacity.
sub_claims.finding: He has worked in tandem with Witkoff on Gaza, Iran (including Geneva talks) and Russia-Ukraine. The White House calls him 'a volunteer and not serving in any official capacity' who pays his own expenses. Witkoff is a formal employee who filed a disclosure.
Form ADV dated 22 Mar 2026: about $6.16B in regulatory AUM at end-2025 (Bloomberg rounds to $6.2B), about 99% from non-US clients.

sub_claims.statement: Per the NYT, Affinity has been trying to raise $5B, largely from Middle Eastern/Gulf sovereign funds.
sub_claims.finding: The NYT reported in March 2026, citing five people, that Kushner was seeking '$5 billion or more'. Affinity had met PIF, and other Gulf funds were expected to be approached. Axios said the fund was not formally in market and that PIF held 'first look' rights. This was a solicitation; it has not been confirmed as a completed raise.

sub_claims.statement: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund put $2B into Affinity and is one of its biggest investors.
sub_claims.finding: PIF committed $2B in mid-2021, overruling its own screening panel's objections (NYT, 2022). It is Affinity's largest investor. QIA and Abu Dhabi's Lunate added about $1.5B in Dec 2024.

sub_claims.statement: Because he holds no official title, Kushner is not subject to divestment requirements and does not have to file financial disclosures.
sub_claims.finding: He has filed no disclosure and has not divested. 'Not subject to' is the White House position. CREW argues he is at least a special government employee who must file, and it sued in Oct 2026. Kushner's lawyer Chad Mizelle says ethics attorneys found his arrangements compliant. No ruling yet.

sub_claims.statement: In closed-door meetings it is unknown whether he argues for the US government or for his own Gulf-backed financial interests.
sub_claims.finding: It is documented that he sought Gulf sovereign money while negotiating in the region, and Wyden and Garcia opened an inquiry on 19 Mar 2026. No evidence has surfaced that he advanced his own interests in any specific negotiation. This is framed as a question and amounts to insinuation.

corrections: Claimed: PIF is 'one of his biggest investors'. The record shows: it is Affinity's largest single investor ($2B, 2021). QIA and Lunate are also investors (about $1.5B, Dec 2024).

Claimed: he is 'not subject to divestment requirements' and need not file disclosures. The record shows: that is the White House's position, which CREW contests in litigation filed Oct 2026, and no court has ruled.
The $5B was a fundraising effort reported by the NYT (March 2026), not a completed raise; headlines saying 'raised $5B' overstate it.
denials_and_context: White House: Kushner is a volunteer, serves in no official capacity, takes no salary and pays his own expenses.

Chad Mizelle (Kushner's lawyer / Affinity chief legal officer): outside and government ethics attorneys reviewed his 'volunteer government service' and found it compliant; the CREW suit is 'without merit'.
In Dec 2024 Kushner said Affinity had 'preemptively tried to avoid any conflicts, so we don't have to raise capital for the next four years'; the 2026 effort contradicts that pledge.

The Daily Beast (citing Bloomberg) reported that Affinity later dropped its planned new fundraising vehicle and will not take new capital while Kushner serves; this is undated in the available coverage and not independently confirmed.
Earlier NYT reporting relayed by The Media Line said Qatar and main Emirati funds declined to invest in a round; this conflicts with the 2024 QIA/Lunate investment and may refer to a different round.

changes: No factual changes. The CREW suit (filed about 14-15 Oct 2026) is confirmed. It also brings an Appointments Clause claim, seeks his removal or at least disclosure filings, and names Susie Wiles, Marco Rubio and Pete Hegseth in their official capacities. I found no ruling as of mid-Nov 2026. The Form ADV figures and Chad Mizelle's response match. Bloomberg's prior filings showed $4.8B for 2024 and $3B for 2023.
